mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the discount rate applied to expected corporate earnings, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 5.25% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 8-week pre-trend period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in manufacturing production (INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which suppresses equity risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day backtest shows no significant negative relationship between the combined labor signal and SPX returns (R^2 < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 8% month-over-month suggests accelerating household demand for housing, which is proxy for broader consumer confidence and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day rolling returns show no correlation with the HOUST signal (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints that reduce future earnings growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During the same 20-day window, SPX outperforms the S&P 500 5-year monthly return by more than 2 standard deviations.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) crosses above 3% for the first time in a rising trend, it signals a shift toward higher real interest rates, which typically precedes a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 months
regime_hint: inflation accelerating toward central bank targets
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite the inflation crossing (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies) and a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) would typically signal a tight labor market, but since we lack openings data, this sketch uses a proxy: when PAYEMS rises while UNRATE falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same month, it suggests conflicting labor signals that are associated with negative 5-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: Over 30 such conflicting labor signals, SPX 5-day returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A regime where both FEDFUNDS is above 5% and UNRATE is below 4% for two consecutive months creates a high-growth, low-inflation environment that historically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no outperformance relative to the pre-signal period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in retail sales (not directly observable; using HOUST as proxy) of 10% over three months suggests consumer demand softening that reduces earnings visibility and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During the 20-day window following the decline, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically worse than during the prior 60-day trend (t-test p > 0.05).
